title: northshore-insurance-integration-call-notes-2026-06-28
content:
Call: Northshore Insurance - Integration scoping
Date: 2026-06-28
Attendees: Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood Solutions), Lena (Northshore IT lead), Mark (Northshore Cloud Eng), Julie (Procurement)

High level:
- Northshore wants Private deployment (VPC + customer-managed control plane) for PII-sensitive workflows (claims triage, fraud detection).
- Pilot scope: 2 services (claims triage chat endpoint + embeddings for legal doc search). Target 6-week pilot.
- Key constraints: data residency in us-east-1 only, SOC2 + HIPAA considerations, strict egress rules, approved HSM/KMS for key management.

Notes / requirements heard:
- Network: will require VPC peering or PrivateLink. They prefer VPC peering into their account. Need clear IP ranges and a network diagram.
- Auth: want integration with their Okta SSO for admin console + LDAP for user groups.
- Keys: customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS with BYOK). HSM optional but they have a procurement preference for HSM-backed CMKs.
- Audit: long retention for audit logs (90 days minimum), logs need to land in their Splunk/CloudWatch; want TLS1.3 enforced and mTLS between control plane and nodes.
- Models: they expect to pin to an open LLM variant we host (rwd-7b-v1-q4 recommended). Will want ability to roll forward to safer model if regressions occur.
- Cost/Throughput: batch workloads for embeddings (bulk ingest nightly), low-latency for chat (p99 < 400ms target) - they emphasized sub-500ms for UX.
- Data handling: claims attachments (PDFs) will be uploaded to their S3 and processed via a connector; need guarantee that raw PII never leaves their VPC.

Gotchas / blockers mentioned:
- Legal wants explicit EULA clauses re: model training/data usage. We must confirm we do not use customer data to train public models; provide a signed assurance.
- Procurement: long lead time (~6-8 weeks) for HSM contract addendum. Pilot timeline might slip unless we accept temporary KMS with stricter contractual terms.
- Networking approval: Northshore's security team is strict about opening peering routes; will require our infra/network diagram and list of CIDR ranges asap.

Actions / Next steps (owners):
- Priya: send network diagram + required ports/CIDR + example VPC peering steps. (Due: 2026-07-01)
- Evan: draft pilot SOW + pilot success metrics (throughput, latency, accuracy for triage). Share by 2026-07-05.
- Lena & Mark: confirm KMS/HSM procurement timeline and whether BYOK with AWS KMS is acceptable or HSM is mandatory. (Lena to confirm by 2026-07-06)
- Mark: share sample S3 ingestion flow and IAM roles required for connector. (Due: 2026-07-03)
- Priya/Evan: prepare a minimal security pack (SOC2 summary, encryption at rest/in transit, audit log retention options) and a short note on data usage policy to satisfy Legal. (Due: 2026-07-02)

Open questions (need answers from Northshore):
- Do they require on-prem (air-gapped) option for pilot or is VPC/private-cloud sufficient?
- Exact SLOs for chat beyond p99 latency (error budget tolerances).
- Are there any approval gates for allowed model families (e.g., no 3rd-party LLMs)?
- Who will be the single technical point-of-contact for network cutover?

Risk notes / tradeoffs (internal):
- If they insist on HSM immediately, pilot timeline likely slips; consider offering staged approach: KMS for pilot + HSM for production.
- Achieving sub-400ms p99 will require careful batching config + model selection (rwd-7b-v1-q4 seems a balanced option), but we should validate on their average prompt size.
- Logging retention forwarding to their Splunk will add egress cost; flag to Finance for SOW.

Prep for follow-up call (deliverables to have ready):
- Sample VPC peering checklist + network diagram (Priya)
- Pilot SOW draft + success metrics + rough pricing band for 6-week pilot (Evan)
- Security pack + data usage statement (Priya + Evan)

Quick rough timeline suggestion:
- Week 0: finalize SOW + network steps + legal review prep
- Week 1: infra setup (VPC peering, KMS access), config private control plane
- Week 2: deploy base model + connectors, run smoke tests
- Week 3-4: pilot traffic ramp, monitoring + observe latency/cost metrics
- Week 5-6: evaluate results, iterate, decide production roll or HSM procurement

Misc notes (scratch):
- Julie (procurement) asked about 3rd party SLAs and support tiers - highlight Dedicated SLA and premium on-call option.
- They are anxious about token-level cost; show Optimize suggestions (batching + prefix cache) in pilot to control spend.
- Ask Legal if we can provide a one-page attestation re: no-training-of-customer-data (fast win).

Tagged follow-ups:
- create JIRA: NS-183 pilot SOW
- add Confluence page under NS integration space with network diagram + access checklist
- schedule next sync: 2026-07-07 (tentative)

Notes to self: keep record of requested CIDRs and ensure SRE ok with peering pattern before sending diagram. Keep messaging simple for Legal (one-pager). Prioritize KMS options in SOW so procurement can move fast.
